target.title: fix(slack): preserve interaction thread status
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Slack interactive button/select follow-up turns could lose their assistant thread when Slack supplied `message.thread_ts` without `container.thread_ts`. The heartbeat turn then had no native Slack assistant status, making a working action look idle.

Fixes #82886.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Preserve the message-level thread timestamp as a fallback while retaining container precedence.
- Add Slack-owned heartbeat status through `assistant.threads.setStatus`.
- Resolve routed `user:<id>` targets through Slack's existing bounded DM-channel cache, covering Assistant DMs without a `conversations.open` request on every keepalive.
- Keep status best-effort so Slack API failures do not block reply delivery.

The contributor branch was rewritten onto current `main` after maintainer review found that the original channel-only helper skipped direct-message routes. Contributor credit is preserved in the replacement commit.

## User Impact

After a user clicks an interactive Slack control in an assistant thread, OpenClaw keeps the correct thread context and shows then clears Slack's native working status for both channel and routed DM targets.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/slack/src/channel.test.ts extensions/slack/src/monitor/events/interactions.test.ts extensions/slack/src/send.upload.test.ts` — 113 tests passed.
- Live configured Slack Assistant DM — the patched `slackPlugin.heartbeat` received a `user:` target, resolved the concrete DM, set status, and cleared it; no test message was posted.
- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kwqh4jcam2449af3dyc5y6x0` — extension production types, extension-test types, lint, repository guards, and runtime import cycles passed. [Actions run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28720467672)
- Fresh structured autoreview — no actionable findings after the Testbox-discovered test fixture type correction.
- `git diff --check` — clean.
